prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit supplied Warline Capture concept board into a new design D, "D · HORIZONTAL PORTRAIT STRIP".
This is a high-fidelity game UI design comparison based on existing actual Campaign HUD. Preserve recognizable desert town, existing heavy squared typography, ARIA cyan hologram with green ARIA PLAY, resources, minimap, and colorful command controls. TWO landscape screenshots stacked with same viewport size. External board labels outside screenshots only: "3 SQUADS" above first, "8 SQUADS · SCROLLABLE" above second. Subtitle "Large images. One continuous strip." Footer outside screenshots: "Swipe the portraits. Tap a squad to select."
Core request: Single horizontal scrolling image-first squad strip at lower left. NO additional header, toolbar, counter, selection-summary bar, pagination dots, arrow button, scrollbar track, category tabs, or labels above or below the strip inside gameplay. Remove old 1–5 of 8 pager completely and restore battlefield behind it. Only actual portrait cards, with thin borders and tight gutters. The strip has no big container background extending into unoccupied space.
Card dimensions identical in both screens: width about 16% of viewport, height about 34% of viewport, tall near-square portrait image. Art fills 90% of card. Tiny stable number badge top-left, short readable footer label over translucent gradient at very bottom, hairline green health strip; cyan outline plus small check for selected 01. No large separate black name block. No empty placeholder cards or excessive padding. Preserve image proportions, crop to fill.
TOP screen contains exactly 3 cards, 01 rifle soldiers, 02 tank, 03 helicopter. Left aligned, each about 16% of viewport width, strip ends immediately after card03, spare space is battlefield. NO stretching to use available width.
BOTTOM screen is a roster of 8 but in the scroll viewport show exactly FOUR complete large cards 01 02 03 04 and the LEFT THIRD of card05 at right edge. The clipped card05 is deliberate and unmistakable: natural viewport crop, subtle edge fade confined to its rightmost edge, never shrink card05 to fit. Cards06–08 are offscreen. Same exact width/height as the three top cards. This visible partial next portrait alone signals horizontal swiping. NO pager or arrows. The card strip is 71% of viewport width, cannot overlap commands.
Both screens have identical fixed colorful command pad at bottom right, within rightmost 27% viewport: top row SELECT MOVE ATTACK HOLD; bottom row SCAN SUPPORT BUILD. Large white icons and short labels, existing game colors. Minimap above. Card strip and command pad align bottom to same safe margin. ARIA retains visible mission goal and next player action. Resource bar stays at screen top; user's 'no extra bars at top' refers to squad strip chrome.
Use production quality clean UI and large attractive illustrated portraits from reference; no additional gameplay systems. The main visual difference between screenshots is number of squad portraits, not their size or arrangement. Do not introduce a gallery or second row.
behavior: One to five squads use capped, fixed-aspect cards; no stretching to fill empty space.
Overflow scrolls horizontally with inertia and gentle card alignment; partial next card communicates more content.
No roster heading, count bar, pager, dots, arrows or permanent scrollbar.
Drag scrolls without selecting or issuing commands; tap selects.
Clip the scroll viewport before the command pad; exact geometry remains implementation work.
